headline: Election Commission Updates Model Code For Retired State Officials
metaDescription: The Election Commission of India has mandated that retired government officials hired by states must follow political neutrality rules during elections.
aiSummaryBullets: The Election Commission of India has expanded model code of conduct restrictions to include retired government staff.
These individuals are now required to maintain political neutrality during the electoral process.
Restricted activities include participation in election campaigning or canvassing for candidates.
aiContextParagraph: The Election Commission of India has issued a directive clarifying the applicability of the Model Code of Conduct to retired government officials who are currently engaged by state governments. This policy adjustment stipulates that such personnel must adhere to strict standards of political neutrality. Under these new guidelines, retired officials are prohibited from involving themselves in election-related campaigns or participating in active canvassing activities. The regulatory body stated that this expansion is intended to ensure fairness and impartiality during the electoral process. By bringing these contractually engaged individuals under the same ethical framework as current government employees, the commission aims to prevent potential conflicts of interest. The update reinforces existing protocols designed to maintain a level playing field for all political participants throughout the campaign period and subsequent voting stages in India.
whyItIsViral: The story has gained visibility through multiple independent media reports, reflecting a moderate level of interest in updated administrative election regulations.
